To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
serum levels of IGSF-I, IGF-I, and IGF-II are decreased and that of IGFBP2 are increased in children with leukaemia.
serum levels of IGP-I, IGFII and IGFBP3 are decreased in children with ALL, while serum levels of IGFP2 are increased.
the serum levels of IGSF-I, IGF-2 and IGFPB-3 are decreased and IGFBP2 levels are increased in children with ALL at the time of diagnosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the IGF regulatory system during childhood leukaemia and the potential use of IGFs, IGFBPs and their receptors as prognostic markers in childhood leukaemia. © 1998 Cancer Research Campaign.
the regulation of the IGF system during childhood cancer, with the aim to elucidate whether this may be of importance to growth failure and tumour growth.
the IGF system in children with leukaemia, with a focus on IGFBP-1, -2 and -3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IGF/IGFBP system is not involved in the pathogenesis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, but that it may be involved in the pathophysiology of growth failure in these patients.
IGFs and IGF binding proteins may be of importance as a growth regulatory pathway in leukemogenesis.
the IGF/IGFBP system in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
serum levels of IGBPs may be of importance in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood leukaemia.
IGFBP-1, IGFBP 2, and IGFBP 3 may be useful as markers to predict response to chemotherapy and/or relapse in childhood ALL.
the IGF regulatory system may have a role in the proliferation of malignant cells and that serum levels of IGH-I and IGF-I may be of prognostic value in leukaemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proliferation of lymphocytes is dependent on IGF-I, -II and IGFBP binding proteins, and that the production of these factors may be impaired in children with ALL.

serum IGFBP-1 levels were significantly higher in the group with a poor prognosis than in those with a good prognosis, which may be an independent prognostic factor for the prognosis of patients with acute myelocytic leukemia.
serum levels of ICF-I, IGF-I, IGFBP2 and IGFB3 are decreased at the time of diagnosis of ALL, and increase during remission.
